Series::cbrt¶

Back to Series API Reference

Signature¶

Series::cbrt() const -> Series
Series& Series::cbrt_()

What It Does¶

cbrt() is the real cube root, applied elementwise.

The key difference from pow(x, 1.0/3.0) is the negative branch. Cube root is defined for every real number — cbrt(-8) = -2, because (-2)^3 = -8 — but pow() with a fractional exponent treats a negative base as a domain error and returns NaN. cbrt() gives the real root across the whole line.

An integer input is promoted to a floating-point result.

Parameters¶

None.

Returns¶

Series or Series& The real cube root elementwise, defined for negatives as well as non-negatives. cbrt_() overwrites the current storage.

Gradient¶

cbrt() is differentiable. Writing y = cbrt(x):

d/dx cbrt(x) = 1 / (3 * x^(2/3)) = 1 / (3 * y^2)

The curve has a vertical tangent at x = 0, so the derivative there is +inf. Everywhere else it is a positive, decreasing function of |x|.

Examples¶

Example 1. Cube root of a negative, zero, and a positive.

pluss::series::print(std::cout, pluss::make_series({-8.0, 0.0, 27.0}).cbrt());

Output¶

Series(shape=[3], strides=[1], dtype=float64, platform=cpu, numel=3, contiguous=true)
data=[-2.0000, 0.0000, 3.0000]

pow(-8.0, 1.0/3.0) would give NaN for the first entry; cbrt() gives -2.

Example 2. The backward multiplier is 1 / (3 * y^2).

auto x = pluss::make_series({1.0, 8.0, 27.0});
x.tracks_slope_(true);

x.cbrt().sum().reverse();

std::cout << "dx=" << x.sensitivity();

Output¶

dx=pluss::Series(shape=[3], strides=[1], dtype=float64, platform=cpu, numel=3, contiguous=true)
data=[0.33333333, 0.083333333, 0.037037037]

For y = 1, 2, 3 the derivative is 1/3, 1/12, 1/27.

Example 3. At x = 0 the tangent is vertical, so the gradient is +inf.

auto x = pluss::make_series({0.0, 1.0});
x.tracks_slope_(true);

x.cbrt().sum().reverse();

std::cout << "dx=" << x.sensitivity();

Output¶

dx=pluss::Series(shape=[2], strides=[1], dtype=float64, platform=cpu, numel=2, contiguous=true)
data=[inf, 0.33333333]

Gotchas And Failure Modes¶

  • The gradient at x = 0 is +inf. A tracked cbrt() on values that can reach 0 produces non-finite sensitivities there.

  • The result is floating point even for an integer input.

  • NaN propagates.

Summary¶

cbrt(x) is the real cube root:

  • defined for negatives, unlike pow(x, 1.0/3.0)

  • promotes integer input to floating point

  • differentiable, backward multiplier 1 / (3 * cbrt(x)^2), +inf at 0

See Also¶

  • Series::pow: the general power, which returns NaN for a negative base with a fractional exponent.

  • Series::sqrt: the square root, defined only on non-negative input.
